description.narrative: The South Tarawa Renewable Energy Project (STREP or the Project) will support upscaling of solar power generation in Kiribati. The Project will reduce dependence on fossil fuel imports by increasing the renewable energy (RE) percentage of electricity generation. STREP has three outputs: (i) solar photovoltaic and battery energy storage system installed; (ii) draft energy act to enable increased deployment of renewable energy developed; and (iii) institutional capacity for inclusive renewable energy project development and implementation enhanced.

Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Institutional capacity for inclusive renewable energy project development and implementation enhanced Indicator: At least 10 technicians (qualified electricians or licensed electrical, mechanical, civil engineers), including at least two women, who received certified training on solar photovoltaic and BESS design, installation, operation, and maintenance are employed in PUB Progress/Status: 3a. Partially achieved. PUB has created a new permanent position and employed a newly graduated female electrical engineer, who currently serves as the BESS Engineer. As confirmed in the BTOR and MOU, certified training for PUB technicians has not yet commenced and remains linked to ongoing construction and commissioning of the solar PV and BESS systems, now expected in Q2 2026. Training is planned to be delivered during construction and commissioning, after which additional technicians (including at least two women) are expected to be trained and retained by PUB.
Data Source: MISE and PUB annual reports; and quarterly project progress reports Actual value:

Output: Institutional capacity for inclusive renewable energy project development and implementation enhanced Indicator: At least 40 stakeholders, including at least 30% women, participate in two national workshops and report increased awareness on photovoltaic and BESS technology Progress/Status: 3d. To be achieved. Will be achieved once constructions start. Planning is still ongoing. These workshops are expected to be conducted during the construction and commissioning phase of the solar PV and BESS systems. Data Source: MISE and PUB annual reports; and quarterly project progress reports Actual value:

Output: Institutional capacity for inclusive renewable energy project development and implementation enhanced Indicator: At least five vocational students, including at least one woman, receive on-the-job training at PUB and MISE for technical or information-technology-related positions Progress/Status: 3b. Women continue to be underrepresented in technical fields, with most female students enrolled in business, community services, accounting, and nursing courses. Efforts are ongoing to encourage female participation in technical training opportunities. Data Source: MISE and PUB annual reports; and quarterly project progress reports Actual value:

Output: Institutional capacity for inclusive renewable energy project development and implementation enhanced Indicator: Project management unit with at least 30% women staff established and operational Progress/Status: 3c. The PMU is established and operational. Women are engaged in PMU and project management functions, including dedicated gender roles and designated gender focal points, as confirmed in the BTOR. However, the proportion of women staff relative to the 30% target has not been formally quantified in the BTOR or MOU. Data Source: MISE and PUB annual reports; and quarterly project progress reports Actual value:

Output: Solar photovoltaic and battery energy storage system installed Indicator: At least 50% of workers engaged by the contractor and PUB in photovoltaic and BESS construction, installation, operation, and maintenance are women Progress/Status: A gender staff member at the PMU and a contractor-based communication and gender officer (joined Nov 2024) support GAP deliverables. PUB's HR Development Officer serves as gender focal point. Total gender indicators: 21, of which 11 (52%) achieved; 4 require attention. For the target of 50% women workers in construction, 28% (15 of 53 workers) are women. Remaining evidence is pending to substantiate some indicators. Key achievements include: (i) PUB's new Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion Policy promoting women's engagement and gender-sensitive recruitment; (ii) 55% women's participation in public consultations and awareness-raising activities, exceeding the 50% target; (iii) 50% women's participation in energy efficiency awareness programs in collaboration with MISE. Data Source: MISE and PUB annual reports, quarterly project progress reports Actual value:

Output: Solar photovoltaic and battery energy storage system installed Indicator: At least two mandatory awareness workshops and trainings for all project staff and contract workers on gender-sensitive renewable energy project design, installation, operation, and maintenance conducted upon mobilization and after commissioning, with at least 30% women participants Progress/Status: Yet to be achieved. Full workshop/training sessions are pending as major construction and commissioning activities are still in progress. The PV system is near completion, while BESS installation and substation works are delayed, with full commissioning now expected in Q2 2026. Preparations are in place, including gender focal points at the PMU and contractor support staff, to conduct the workshops for all staff and contract workers once mobilization and commissioning milestones are reached. Data Source: MISE and PUB annual reports, quarterly project progress reports Actual value:

Output: Solar photovoltaic and battery energy storage system installed Indicator: At least two public awareness programs conducted on efficient electricity demand management targeting women, youth, and church organizations (Target: 50% women) Progress/Status: In collaboration with MISE, the project conducted community awareness and outreach programs, including roadshows and distribution of energy-efficiency leaflets. Women's participation reached 50%, meeting the target. Data Source: MISE and PUB annual reports, quarterly project progress reports Actual value:

Output: Draft energy act to enable increased deployment of renewable energy developed Indicator: Draft energy act, which includes restructured tariff policy, based on gender-sensitive tariff review and gender review of Kiribati Energy Policy, PUB Statement of Intent (Strategic Plan), and Recruitment Policy, submitted by MISE to Parliament Progress/Status: Significant progress has been achieved under Output 2, marked by the enactment of the Energy Act in December 2024, which lays the foundation for a more robust policy and regulatory framework for Kiribati's energy sector. The regulations developed under STREP are essential for the implementation of the Energy Act. They are designed to support the functions of MISE and to regulate the activities of all stakeholders in the electricity sector, including generators, distributors, and end users.
Output 2 targets are expected to be met with minor revision only. Specifically, the gender mainstreaming provisions, recommended in the draft final Energy Act, were not included in the approved legislation. To address this gap, the Mission discussed with MISE the inclusion of gender mainstreaming provisions in the Renewable Energy Regulations, which are being drafted.
Data Source: Ministry of Finance and Economic Development, MISE, PUB annual reports; project progress reports Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: Not Applicable Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: Not Applicable Target year: 2027 Target value: Yes

Output: Draft energy act to enable increased deployment of renewable energy developed Indicator: Technical standards on renewable-energy-related electrical equipment, which follow New Zealand and Australian standards, developed Progress/Status: The Energy Performance Labelling and Testing Regulation was endorsed in April 2024. However, implementation is pending the formal appointment of a commencement date by the MISE Minister. This is expected to progress once the Senior Energy Efficiency Planner is successfully recruited—currently underway. Output: Solar photovoltaic and battery energy storage system installed Indicator: At least 5 MW/13 MWh of BESS commissioned and operational Progress/Status: Solar PV nearly complete (~98% panels, 85% DC cables, 100% inverters, 90% PV transformers; PV transformer 1-2 cabling done). BESS behind schedule: modules/PCS delivered, ~20% foundation completed; full installation pending BESS transformer delivery in early Q1 2026. Substation 20% complete; equipment delivery Jan-Mar 2026; commissioning of PV and BESS now expected Q2 2026. Data Source: MISE and PUB annual reports, quarterly project progress reports Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: 0 Target year: 2027 Target value: 5 MW/13 MWh

Output: Solar photovoltaic and battery energy storage system installed Indicator: At least an additional 5.000 MWp photovoltaic capacity commissioned and operational Progress/Status: Installation of the solar PV system is largely complete, with 98% of panels, 85% of DC cabling, 100% of inverters, and 90% of PV transformers installed. However, commissioning of at least 5.000 MWp of photovoltaic capacity has been delayed due to slower progress in BESS and substation works. While BESS modules and PCS units have been delivered, only about 20% of foundation works have been completed, and delivery of BESS transformers is now expected in early Q1 2026. Substation (MV building) construction is also delayed (20% completed), with key equipment scheduled for delivery between January and March 2026. Installation of substation equipment is expected to be completed in early Q2 2026, enabling commissioning of the solar PV and BESS systems later in the same quarter. Data Source: MISE and PUB annual reports, quarterly project progress reports Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: 1.565 MWp Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: 1.565 MWp Target year: 2027 Target value: additional 5 MWp PV

Contractor engagement is complete; O&M services and related training will be delivered as planned after commissioning.
